{"total_count":1,"workflow_runs":[{"id":35115890405,"name":"CI","display_title":"Switch the site's host from GitHub Pages to Cloudflare","workflow_id":318294478,"run_number":327,"run_attempt":1,"event":"pull_request","status":"completed","conclusion":"success","head_branch":"claude/friendly-cannon-4h2pf8","head_sha":"dd2e90a0883bf43aadd96d51ef2e677af0c09fce","head_commit":{"message":"Switch the site's host from GitHub Pages to Cloudflare

Adopts the cloudflare-site pack and undeclares static-website. The two cannot
both hold: static-website moves the version with the change and releases on push
to main, while cloudflare-site has its nightly site-release task cut the version
itself and upload the tree — so sw/version-bumped would demand a per-PR bump the
new model does not want.

wrangler.jsonc names site/ as the published tree and claims both hostnames as
custom domains. Two of its keys are set against Cloudflare's documented
defaults rather than left alone:

  - workers_dev defaults to TRUE, which would publish this same site a second
    time at edfringenow.<account>.workers.dev — a public URL nobody chose.
  - not_found_handling defaults to a bare, body-less 404. Pages answered an
    unknown path with a real page, so site/404.html keeps that promise; it is
    the one page whose URLs are root-relative, because Cloudflare serves it
    under whatever path the visitor actually asked for.

assets.directory uploads everything beneath it, which is wider than the Pages
publish set was: that list named plan/ file by file to keep the design mock out,
and could not exclude the __tests__ dirs it shipped. site/.assetsignore replaces
the enumeration and drops both — 113 files become 84. Its patterns were checked
against real gitignore semantics, which is what wrangler matches with.

The version moves onto the pack's generated stamp. There is no build step in the
release — it uploads the committed tree verbatim — so a published version.json
had nothing to write it. Each page now carries title="version <n>", stamped from
package.json by the pack's bump and guarded against drift by a check, and
shared/version.js reads it. The reader takes the attribute with it: title is
painted by the browser, and this site deliberately replaced that tooltip with a
styled popup it can position and screenshot. The harness pins the stamp, so the
goldens record the product rather than the day they were rendered.

Retires the five static-site-* workflows, site.config and the three composite
actions. scripts/build-site.sh goes with them: the beacon injection is the
release worker's now, and js/build-info.js was written by the deploy and read by
nothing. No canon pack owns generic CI, so ci.yml is the repo's own — it runs
scripts/verify.sh and nothing else, and deliberately does not dry-run wrangler,
which no-second-publisher refuses in any workflow.

Corrects what the switch falsifies. The caching comments said the host offered
no way to vary Cache-Control per file; Cloudflare does (_headers), but serves
assets must-revalidate with an ETag — so the client cache still earns its place,
for a different reason than the one written down.

Closes #733
Refs #734

content.text: Both lanes passed on the first commit, but no run exists yet for the major-bump head. Let me confirm the push landed and re-poll.

{"number":735,"title":"Switch the site's host from GitHub Pages to Cloudflare","body":"Step 2 of the migration. #731 moved the site into `site/`; this swaps the host.

Closes #733

## The pack swap

Adopts `cloudflare-site` through the canon install runner and **undeclares `static-website`**. The two cannot both hold: `static-website` moves the version with the change and releases on push to `main`, while `cloudflare-site` has its nightly `site-release` task cut the version itself and upload the tree — so `sw/version-bumped` would demand a per-PR bump the new model does not want.

## Two config keys set against Cloudflare's defaults

Both verified against Cloudflare's own docs, not assumed:

- **`workers_dev` defaults to `true`** — left alone it would publish this same site a second time at `edfringenow.<account>.workers.dev`, a public URL nobody chose, serving the product under a name that is not the product's.
- **`not_found_handling` defaults to a bare, body-less 404.** Pages answered an unknown path with a real page (9,379 bytes, checked against the live site), so `site/404.html` keeps that promise. It is the one page whose URLs are **root-relative**: Cloudflare serves its bytes under whatever path the visitor actually asked for, so a page-relative `css/styles.css` would resolve against that unknown path and 404 in turn, leaving an unstyled error page.

Deliberately **not** `single-page-application` — this site is four pages plus three planners, and answering every unknown path with `index.html` would serve the Now page under any URL a visitor mistyped.

## The publish boundary got wider, so `.assetsignore` narrows it

`assets.directory` uploads *everything* beneath it. That is wider than the Pages publish set, which enumerated `plan/` file by file to keep the design mock out and could not exclude the `__tests__` dirs it knowingly shipped. `site/.assetsignore` replaces that enumeration: **113 files become 84.**

I verified the patterns rather than trusting the syntax — wrangler matches with the `ignore` npm package (gitignore semantics, and it auto-ignores `.assetsignore`, `_redirects` and `_headers` itself), so I tested the exact pattern set against real gitignore matching. All four `__tests__` dirs, the design mock and the two stray docs drop; no product file moves.

## The version moves onto the pack's stamp

The release has **no build step** — it uploads the committed tree verbatim — so the `site/version.json` that #731 introduced had nothing to write it. Each page now carries `title="version <n>"`, stamped from `package.json` by the pack's own bump and guarded against drift by a check; `site/shared/version.js` reads it.

The reader **takes the attribute with it**, because this repo deliberately moved the version *off* a native `title` tooltip — the browser paints those outside the page, so they can't be styled, keyboard-reached or screenshotted for the gallery (see `version-popup.js`). The stamp is a build-time carrier; the styled popup stays the UI.

The harness pins the stamp so the goldens record the product rather than the day they were rendered. The major bump below is the first real test of that, and all 110 stayed pixel-identical across it.

## The major goes to 2

The two packs date a version differently — `<major>.<ymmdd>.<n>` against `<major>.<mmdd>.<n>` — so the first Cloudflare release off `1.60916.2` would have cut `1.0916.3`, a middle number that visibly shrinks. The major absorbs it, the same move the scheme makes for its own decade wrap: `1.60916.2` becomes **`2.0916.2`** (the same release, renumbered — same date, same counter), and the first release cuts `2.0917.3`.

The page stamps come from the pack's own `--stamp-only` bump, which consumes no version number, rather than by hand.

## What got retired

content.text:
Here's what the switch touches, folder by folder:

```
wrangler.jsonc     new — names site/ as the published tree, claims both hostnames,
                   and turns OFF workers_dev (defaults on, would have published the
                   site a second time at a *.workers.dev URL nobody chose)

site/              .assetsignore narrows the upload back down (113 files → 84: the
                   four __tests__ dirs, the design mock, two stray docs);
                   404.html is new, root-relative because Cloudflare serves it under
                   whatever path was asked for; shared/version.js reads the release
                   stamp out of the page and strips the attribute so the native
                   tooltip this repo deliberately removed stays gone; the three
                   pages carry that stamp and version.json is deleted

.github/           the five static-site-* workflows, site.config and the three
                   composite actions are gone; ci.yml replaces them, running
                   scripts/verify.sh and nothing else; the executor now passes the
                   two Cloudflare secrets through to the release task

scripts/           build-site.sh deleted — the beacon injection is the release
                   worker's now, and the build stamp it wrote was read by nothing

product/           the harness serves pages through a pinned stamp, so a release
                   can't churn the goldens; the version.json fixture is gone

.claudinite/       cloudflare-site vendored, static-website undeclared
```

**Release and live check, done first.** [PR #731](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/731) merged, cut `v1.60916.2`, deployed. I checked it properly rather than trusting the green run: every published path serves at its old URL, the three pipeline files (`data/prices.json`, the 7.4 MB master, `package.json`) correctly 404, and the live page renders `v1.60916.2` in its footer.

**Two things I'd flag from the Cloudflare work:**

Cloudflare's asset default is `max-age=0, must-revalidate` + ETag. The client cache's comments said the host gave no way to vary headers per file — Cloudflare *does* (`_headers`), so the stated reason was wrong while the conclusion stayed right. Both comments now say the true one; no caching behaviour moved. Worth knowing `_headers` exists if that policy is ever revisited.

I couldn't verify `.assetsignore` from the docs, and `--dry-run` can't answer it either — its "Read N files" is pre-filter and counts directories (4 files + 2 dirs = 6, which is how I worked it out). So I read the pinned wrangler's own bundle: it uses the `ignore` package, plain gitignore semantics. Then I tested the exact patterns against real gitignore matching rather than shipping a guess.

**On the version**, your major bump landed, then [#732](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/732) released `1.60916.3` underneath me and conflicted on both `package.json` and the planJerusalem page. Resolved by taking main's side and re-running the pack's `--stamp-only` bump rather than hand-editing a stamp: **`2.0916.3`**, first Cloudflare release cuts `2.0917.4`. That merge was also the real test of the golden pinning — the committed version changed twice and all 115 goldens (main's five new i18n cases included) stayed pixel-identical.

[#734](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/issues/734) is yours: zone, nameservers, two secrets. **The nameserver move takes every record on the domain, mail included** — check Cloudflare's imported list against your registrar's before you flip.

> ⚠️ Still open: [PR #735](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/735) — CI re-running on the merged head; it was green on the previous one and the merge is verified locally (291 tests, 115 goldens). The switch does not take effect until [#734](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/issues/734)'s account steps are done — until then every release parks naming what's missing, which is the intended failure rather than a half-configured deploy.

The Stop hook's merge-commit finding was right, and the fix was worth doing properly rather than trusting it.

**The merge commit is gone.** I'd merged `main` in to resolve the conflict — the canon's PR rules allow that, but this repo squash-merges and `squash-merge-history` blocks a merge commit in the work. Rebased instead, which re-hit the same conflicts plus a new set (commit 1 now stamps `1.60916.3`, so commit 2's diff no longer applied).

I resolved none of the version conflicts by hand — the pack's rule is explicit that a hand-typed stamp names a build that was never served, so every one went through `bump-version.mjs --stamp-only`. Then I checked the result the only way that actually proves it: **the rebased tree hashes identical to the merge-resolved tree I'd already run 291 tests and 115 goldens against** (`816c574` both). Same bytes, linear history. That's why I didn't re-run the UI lane — a bit-identical tree can't render differently.

Loading `working-with-generated-files` confirmed the two GENERATED files were fine (produced by their generators, not hand-edited) and gave me the rule I needed for the rebase: a conflict in one is resolved by re-running the generator. Neither conflicted, as it happened.

**One advisory I'm reporting rather than fixing:** `shared-tree-immutable` fired on all 15 vendored `cloudflare-site` files. Those are the install runner's own output — the check can't tell adopting a pack from hand-editing the mount, so it will fire on *every* pack adoption in *every* member repo. That's a canon-level gap, and the fix belongs in the Claudinite repo, which this session's scope can't reach. Not filing it here: an issue in this queue would park on a repo it can't read. Flagging it to you instead, as the one of those three options that's honest.

On the two question advisories: the layout/domain one was a real fork I couldn't resolve. The version one I'd defend — the repo's own convention makes the major your declaration, never a release's.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. # Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); when the change has an issue,
   the body carries `Closes #<issue>` on its own line.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it
   again. (1)
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read an issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.
